svg.title: UHF RFID band map — the UAE follows the European 865-868 MHz band plus a 915-921 MHz upper band
svg.desc: A frequency map of the UHF RFID bands: the European Union uses 865-868 MHz under ETSI EN 302 208, the United States uses 902-928 MHz under FCC Part 15, and the United Arab Emirates follows the European allocation under the TDRA per ETSI EN 302 208 — a primary 865-868 MHz band at 2 W e.r.p. (four interrogator channels 865.7, 866.3, 866.9 and 867.5 MHz, 200 kHz each; tags respond at -20 dBm e.r.p.) and an upper 915-921 MHz band at 4 W e.r.p. (passive tags 915.3-920.9 MHz with Detect-And-Avoid; interrogators 916.3, 917.5 and 918.7 MHz). The UAE lower band aligns exactly with the EU band, so an EU-tuned 865-868 MHz inlay is band-correct in the UAE, while a US 902-928 MHz-tuned inlay is not the default. Access cards at 13.56 MHz are global.

An EU-tuned 865-868 MHz inlay is band-correct for the UAE; a US 902-928 MHz-tuned inlay is not the default.
Order 865-868 MHz tuning (add the 915-921 MHz upper band only if your readers use it).
Access-control cards at 13.56 MHz (HF) are global and unaffected by the UHF band split.
